mbm-0193.clue: The pancakes come out shaped like the weather.
mbm-0193.quote: I cook them over a camp stove in a dented frying pan. The batter runs toward the dent, so every pancake has a little cloud on one edge. My sister asks for the rainy side.

mbm-0194.clue: Two hands and three clean tea towels.
mbm-0194.quote: I practiced juggling with tea towels because they fall so slowly. I finally kept all three up until the kettle whistled. Nobody could dry the breakfast plates till I was done.

mbm-0195.clue: The green leaf goes on last.
mbm-0195.quote: My aunt finishes every necklace with a green glass leaf. I did it too on my first necklace. She recognized mine across the table before she saw my face.

mbm-0196.clue: You can see the sea from row five.
mbm-0196.quote: I painted waves on a long strip of cloth for our stage crew. When you turn the crank, the sea rolls by. One fish is swimming the wrong way so my friends can spot my work.

mbm-0197.clue: The rope has a yellow duck tied to it.
mbm-0197.quote: We fastened a rubber duck to the dry bag on our raft. It bobbed through the rapids with a much calmer expression than our faces. The crew voted it captain for the paddle home.

mbm-0198.clue: My aunt saved my contest shirt.
mbm-0198.quote: The first spoonful of cherry cobbler landed squarely on my collar. I finished the bowl anyway. My aunt embroidered a green stem over the stain, and now it’s my special shirt.

mbm-0199.clue: The station clock is three minutes kind.
mbm-0199.quote: The early freight always passes before the clock says six. I leave the house with my tea still brewing and make it to the crossing just as the engine shows. The tea steeps through the whole train.

mbm-0200.clue: We put real pockets on the bookshelf quilt.
mbm-0200.quote: At our sewing circle I made a row of fabric books for my niece. Two spines open to hide library cards. She checks out her teddy bear’s favorites with a completely straight face.

mbm-0201.clue: We race to the patch of sunshine.
mbm-0201.quote: In the shallow end at opening time the sun makes one yellow square on the tiles. My brother and I swim to it with our eyes open underwater. By the last lap the finish line’s moved.

mbm-0202.quote: My gran knitted a rabbit to cover my driver. I took it off to tee up and a real rabbit stepped out of the rough. We both waited politely for my turn to end.

mbm-0203.clue: I can hear the bishop coming.
mbm-0203.quote: Our park set is hollow. My opponent put a dry pea inside the bishop after the base came loose. On a quiet morning his longest move sounds like a tiny rainstick.

mbm-0204.clue: We light the lamp for one drawing.
mbm-0204.quote: Before we zip the tent I take one minute to sketch what’s outside. The other night all I got down was a bendy pine tree and one corner of the moon. That’s enough to take me right back.

mbm-0205.clue: Listen for the first two taps.
mbm-0205.quote: I play claves with my uncle’s son group. When his guitar string broke I kept the pulse until he had another string on. The dancers had been doing the repair time with us.

mbm-0206.clue: I brought a clothesline to the desert.
mbm-0206.quote: On our camping trip it didn’t rain once. We used the clothesline to hang little drawings of everything we spotted. The last morning our laundry was twelve birds and a lizard.

mbm-0207.clue: The radio sits on a folded sock.
mbm-0207.quote: I take it down to the sunny steps by the water. The sock tips it just enough for me to hear without bothering anyone. The woman two towels over still taps her foot when the trumpets start.

mbm-0208.clue: I put a red door in every village quilt.
mbm-0208.quote: My grandmother couldn’t remember the street where she learned to ride a bike, but she could describe the red door. I sewed it into a row of little houses and she pointed to it at once.

mbm-0209.clue: Our hiking map has a fold the wrong way round.
mbm-0209.quote: My cousin folded it under her mug to keep it steady on a rock. Now the map pops up like a little tent at exactly the place we stopped for tea.

mbm-0210.clue: I can set a ball with a peach in my pocket.
mbm-0210.quote: We play beach doubles next to a fruit stand. The owner promises the last peach to whoever returns a serve without stepping on the chalk circle. I’ve never watched my toes so closely.

mbm-0211.quote: We flew a cracked Frisbee in the yard and it kept drifting into the lilacs. My brother taped on a penny to balance it. The disc still curves, only now it costs a cent to lose.

mbm-0212.clue: The best part is where the tape comes off.
mbm-0212.quote: I taped rectangles on my painting to leave little sunlit windows. It takes two of us to get the last strip off straight. My dad says it feels just like opening the shutters.

mbm-0213.quote: My family uses a pair of beach bags for cricket stumps. My aunt set her shades on top of one bag and declared it the umpire. We take our appeals to a very cool official.

mbm-0214.clue: I sleep next to a shoe full of newspaper.
mbm-0214.quote: On our first wet camping trip I stuffed the boots with old sports pages. In the morning we sat by the fire trading yesterday’s scores one dry boot at a time.

mbm-0215.clue: There’s an envelope on the back cover.
mbm-0215.quote: I collect tiny paper maps from adventure novels I’ve finished. The envelope in my favorite one holds seven islands now. Sometimes I make up a ferry service between them.

mbm-0216.clue: My ribbon has a sauce stain the shape of a heart.
mbm-0216.quote: I entered the dumpling contest with my dad. He finished first and gave me the last one off his plate. The judge wrote down two times and ordered one extra serving for the ride home.

mbm-0217.clue: You can hear the whole club turn a page.
mbm-0217.quote: We each drew one frame of a cat climbing a drainpipe after the cartoon festival. On my frame the cat looked down. When we flip the book, that one little glance makes everybody catch their breath.
